name: Objects in dither
for: The picture of a real thing when there is no photograph of it: headphones, an office chair, a camera or a drone, built in code as a lit 3D form and printed in ordered dither in the page tones (ground, shade, ink, accent and a deep accent). It sways slowly on its spot; pointed at, it turns to the pointer, the light comes from the pointer and the object answers: sound rings out of the cups, the seat swivels, the lens zooms, the rotors spin up and the drone lifts off.
how: data-cx-object on the figure names the object (headphones, chair, camera, drone); data-cx-label can replace the stage's spoken label. Each is a small signed-distance model in its own shader, mounted with fx.shader (lazy WebGL context, paused off screen and in a hidden tab). The shader runs once per dither cell, not per pixel: the canvas has one pixel per 3 CSS px cell (2 px on a stage under 420px) on every screen and is scaled up pixelated, rays that miss the object skip the march, and it draws 20 frames a second. Under reduced motion it is drawn once and kept as a picture (still: no context). The accent paints one part (the ear cups, the seat and back, the camera's body band, the drone's shell), its shaded side in a deep accent. The stage is the card tone with a 4:3 aspect; a pause button sits in its top-right corner. The print is the render to use. data-cx-render="studio" (a smooth shaded render of the same form) exists but is not for pages yet: at one sample per CSS pixel its edges stair-step and the forms read as toys next to a real product shot. No caption under the stage, ever: the section copy says what it is.
rules: One object per page (one live WebGL context), as the hero picture or the visual of one split section; never two on a page.

Only an object the product really is or sells (headphones for an audio brand, a chair for a furniture maker, a camera for a camera or photo-gear shop, a drone for a drone maker or a survey service that flies them). Never an unrelated object for decoration.
No caption under the stage: the section heading or copy names the object and gives one real fact from the client.
The print render, never studio: studio is not anti-aliased yet.
The object moves inside its stage only; the stage and the card never move, nothing follows scroll.
a11y: The stage is role=img with a label that names the object (data-cx-label to replace it). A pause button holds the sway and the hover answer; reduced motion shows one still picture (no context) and no button. Without WebGL the stage shows a still line drawing of the same object.
